definitions.explanation: Vessels and objects made from clay and fired in a kiln. In the strict sense, refers to earthenware (fired at lower temperatures, somewhat porous) as opposed to porcelain (磁器), but in common usage can refer to ceramics in general.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{陶器|とうき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧だ。
{陶器|とうき}{市|いち}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{気|き}に{入|い}った→気に入る：02047_kiniiru⟧⟦{茶碗|ちゃわん}→茶碗：01019_chawan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought a rice bowl I liked at the pottery market.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{有田焼|ありたやき}→有田焼：28604_aritayaki⟧や{備前焼|びぜんやき}⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な{陶器|とうき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{産地|さんち}→産地：04031_sanchi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たくさん→たくさん：00597_takusan⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Japan has many famous pottery production areas, such as Arita ware and Bizen ware.

notes:
Compound of {陶|とう} (pottery/clay) + {器|き} (vessel/utensil).

Strictly speaking, {陶器|とうき} (earthenware) and ⟦{磁器|じき}→磁器：03335_jiki⟧ (porcelain) are different: {陶器|とうき} is fired at lower temperatures and has a warmer, rougher texture, while ⟦{磁器|じき}→磁器：03335_jiki⟧ is fired at higher temperatures and is smooth and translucent. Together they are called ⟦{陶磁器|とうじき}→陶磁器：15698_toujiki⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {陶器|とうき}{市|いち} (pottery market/fair)
- {陶器|とうき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{皿|さら}→皿：00883_sara⟧ (ceramic plate)
- {陶器|とうき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (to fire pottery)

Famous Japanese pottery styles include ⟦{有田焼|ありたやき}→有田焼：28604_aritayaki⟧, {瀬戸焼|せとやき}, {備前焼|びぜんやき}, and {益子焼|ましこやき}.
